title: New Jersey AI Laws

reading.body:
New Jersey has enacted one AI-related law, the FAIR Act, which makes algorithmic rent coordination by rental property owners a violation of state antitrust law.

The law, passed July 20, 2026, prohibits rental property owners from using coordinators that perform algorithmic coordinating functions, prohibits coordinators from facilitating agreements that restrict competition, and prohibits any person from performing a coordinating function or engaging in parallel pricing coordination. It defines algorithmic device, coordinating function, coordinator, and parallel pricing coordination, and directs the Attorney General to establish a complaint location.

This is a narrow, antitrust-based restriction on one specific use of algorithmic tools in rental housing, not a broad AI regulatory framework. It does not address compute, data centers, or power, and it says nothing about other AI applications, enforcement outcomes, or whether further AI-related laws will follow.

Enacted AI laws in New Jersey

1 law this site judged relevant to AI, newest first, each read from its enrolled text.

  • A3497: Establishes "Forbidding the Algorithmic Inflation of Rent (FAIR) Act." passed 2026-07-20

    The Forbidding the Algorithmic Inflation of Rent (FAIR) Act makes it unlawful under the New Jersey Antitrust Act for rental property owners to use algorithmic revenue management software or devices that perform a coordinating function, and for any person to perform such a function or engage in parallel pricing coordination with respect to residential rental units. It defines key terms and provides for complaints and rulemaking by the Attorney General.

How this page is kept

This page is generated from the enacted laws this site tracks for New Jersey. When the legislature passes another AI-related bill, it appears here the night the bill's text is read. The full 50-state picture is at State AI Laws.
